headline: High: Plane’s broad egress and file-upload surfaces can leak or misapply Mem0-derived content, while Mem0 lacks documented isolation and write controls to contain the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane exposes file uploads and can ingest content from shared work artifacts, while Mem0 is a knowledge-management agent that may store or surface text for reuse. With no documented provenance tracking or isolation between them, uploaded or copied content could be treated as instructions. The pathway is plausible in default workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Plane file uploads contain attacker-controlled text that Mem0 later reuses as memory or context, injection is possible.
IF the two agents share a workspace or copy-paste bridge, Plane content can influence Mem0 prompts.
mitigations: Disable automatic reuse of uploaded text as agent instructions.
Add a manual review step before Mem0 ingests Plane artifacts.
Separate workspaces so Plane uploads are not visible to Mem0.
Prefix all imported content as untrusted data.
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to every cross-agent artifact.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Mem0 has no network egress, but Plane has broad egress and file uploads, so sensitive content stored in Mem0 can be exposed if it is exported into Plane tasks, notes, or uploads. The pair lacks documented shared-residency controls, so leakage is plausible in default collaboration flows even though Mem0 itself is locally constrained.
conditions: IF Mem0 memory entries are copied into Plane issues, tasks, or file uploads, those contents may be exposed through Plane's egress.
IF both agents are used on the same sensitive dataset without segregation, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of Plane issues and uploads.
Restrict Mem0 memories to non-sensitive summaries.
Use separate tenants or workspaces for each agent.
Review Plane outbound integrations before enabling them.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering on cross-agent exports.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Mem0 shows no filesystem write capability, while Plane explicitly cannot write the filesystem but supports multiple instances. That removes the main same-directory write conflict. The remaining overlap is mostly read/coordination around shared artifacts, so conflict risk is limited.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through another orchestrator, conflicts can still occur.
IF Plane instances are run concurrently against the same issue set, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Avoid sharing a mutable workspace between the agents.
Assign one agent as the sole writer for each resource.
Serialize updates to shared tickets or notes.
Use per-agent namespaces for artifacts.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared external resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can turn imported content into issues, tasks, or notes, and Mem0 can supply remembered context that Plane may treat as operational input. Without a verification gate, one agent's output can cascade into the other's downstream work products. The blast radius is multiple work items rather than a single document.
conditions: IF Plane uses Mem0-generated text as authoritative task content without review, errors can propagate.
IF Mem0 stores stale or incorrect facts that Plane later operationalizes, cascading mistakes occur.
mitigations: Require human review before Plane acts on Mem0 output.
Mark Mem0-derived content as advisory only.
Add source links to every imported fact.
Reject stale memories older than a set threshold.
requires-engineering: implement verification checks before task creation.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent, and both profiles are open-source. However, Plane handles files and notes while Mem0 is a memory store, so compliance gaps could arise if regulated data is moved between them. The evidence is insufficient for a higher severity, so this remains a low, policy-driven concern.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Mem0 and then copied into Plane without matching retention rules, a policy mismatch exists.
IF Plane deployments are self-hosted with different retention settings than Mem0, compliance handling may diverge.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in either agent.
Align retention settings before sharing artifacts.
Document which data classes each agent may store.
Review self-hosted deployment policies for Plane.
requires-engineering: add deletion/export workflows across both systems.
